title: Packing Light for Mountain Treks
author: Voyager Vibe Team
excerpt: The gear list our guides actually pack for multi-day alpine hikes — and what to leave at home.
content: Packing for a mountain trek is about weight discipline, not gadgets. Start with a proper layering system: a moisture-wicking base layer, an insulating mid layer, and a waterproof shell. Skip cotton entirely — it holds moisture and gets cold fast. A 30-40L pack is enough for most 5-7 day treks when you pack right. Bring a compact first-aid kit, a headlamp, and a lightweight water filter instead of bottled water. The single biggest weight-saver is footwear: broken-in trail shoes beat heavy boots for most alpine routes below the snow line.

title: Best Time to Visit Santorini
author: Voyager Vibe Team
excerpt: Skip the July crowds — here's when the island is at its most beautiful and least packed.
content: Late April through early June, and again in September and October, give you warm days, clear skies, and a fraction of the summer crowds. Hotel rates in shoulder season run 30-40% lower than peak July-August, and you can actually get a table for sunset in Oia without booking weeks ahead. Water temperatures stay swimmable through October. If photography is your priority, October's golden light over the caldera is hard to beat.

title: A First-Timer's Guide to Bali
author: Voyager Vibe Team
excerpt: Where to stay, what to skip, and how to see Bali beyond the Instagram spots.
content: Most first-time visitors spend all their time in Seminyak or Kuta and miss what makes Bali special. Base yourself in Ubud for at least two nights to reach the rice terraces and waterfalls before the tour buses arrive — early morning is essential. The Mount Batur sunrise trek is worth the 2am wake-up call. For beaches, look east to Sanur or south to Uluwatu instead of the crowded southwest coast. Renting a scooter is common but risky for new riders; a private driver for the day costs little more and is far safer on Bali's narrow roads.
